title: Result Aggregator & Comparison Hub + Anomaly Playbook for Throughput Regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight result aggregator service and a Comparison Hub UI that surfaces tokens/sec, p95 latency, and regression signals across runs, and standardize an ops playbook for triaging anomalies. Scope: storage schema for run metadata and metrics, an efficient compare API to support side-by-side and trend diffs, UI components for run grouping/filtering, and an automated triage workflow that debounces flakiness and attaches rerun artifacts and suspect PRs.
motivation: Current benchmark artifacts are scattered (s3 blobs + ad-hoc CSVs). Engineers spend too long reconstructing runs when a p95/throughput alert fires. We need a single searchable store + comparison surface to shave investigation time and automate first-line triage actions.
proposal_summary: 1) Result Aggregator service that normalizes run outputs into a compact row-per-run format. 2) Comparison Hub: run selector, baseline pinning, metric delta table (tokens/sec, p50, p95, tail-percentiles, failure-rate), and trend sparkline. 3) Regression detector: rolling baseline, percent-delta thresholds, and z-score anomaly flagging with a debounced alert window. 4) Triage playbook automation: auto-rerun on suspect hardware/noise, tag owner, attach likely PRs and relevant Grafana/bench dashboards to the incident card.
storage_schema_notes: Store one canonical run document per job: run_id, commit_sha, model_variant, seq_len_profile_tag, hardware_snapshot, batch_config, tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, error_count, samples_count, histogram_buckets (encoded), run_time_iso, environment_tags. Use a time-partitioned column store (Parquet on S3) with a lightweight Postgres index layer for fast lookups by run_id/commit/model/label. Keep a denormalized metrics table for quick comparators. Retain raw telemetry for 90 days and aggregates for 2 years.
detection_algorithm: Primary rule: mark regression when p95 increases by >= 20% AND tokens/sec decreases by >= 15% relative to pinned baseline across N=3 latest stable runs. Supplement with statistical test: compute rolling median and MAD; flag if current point has z_score > 3 on p95 after log-transform. Debounce: require 2 consecutive failing runs within 24 hours before triggering high-priority alert. Add noise detection: if GPU utilization variance > 15% or a system-level incident tag exists, mark as flaky and auto-schedule rerun instead of alerting.
comparison_api_contract: GET /compare?baseline=<run_id>&candidate=<run_id>&metrics=p95,tokens_sec&window=24h returns JSON flat list: [metric, baseline_value, candidate_value, delta_pct, significance_flag, links_to_raw_samples]. The API must support bulk compare (one baseline vs N candidates) and time-series delta summaries for sparkline rendering.
ui_requirements: Comparison Hub must support: multi-run pinning, auto-group by model_variant or seq_len_profile, highlight regressions (red) and improvements (green), side-by-side histogram overlay, raw-sample download link, quick-jump to rerun action, and a compact triage card that pre-populates suggested owners and likely PRs. Include keyboard shortcuts: 'b' to pin baseline, 'r' to request rerun.
triage_playbook_summary: 1) Alert fires -> create ticket in triage board with prefilled run summary. 2) Automated checks: compare hardware snapshot, compare infra incident tags, compute z-score, and attempt a single rerun on isolated infra. 3) If rerun passes, mark as flaky and close with notes. 4) If rerun fails twice, escalate to on-call SRE + model owner, attach suspect commits and open a regression investigation ticket. 5) Postmortem template link will be attached when severity meets 'high' customer_impact.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator stores runs and returns fast lookups by run_id within 300ms
Comparison API returns delta table and time-series in <500ms for typical baseline vs candidate queries
UI highlights regressions per detection rules and can pin a baseline
Playbook automation performs auto-rerun and tags owner candidate with <= 5 minutes latency from alert
Integration tests exist covering flaky-run debouncing and rerun success/failure flows
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from infra jitter. Mitigation: require consecutive failures + hardware variance check before high-priority alert
Risk: storage cost blowup from retaining raw samples. Mitigation: compress raw traces, shorten raw retention to 90 days and keep aggregates longer
Risk: owners not obvious for cross-repo regressions. Mitigation: attach likely PRs via git blame heuristics and add 'unknown-owner' Slack channel escalation
